facts.fact: Huawei, the vendor, says that under the second phase of the state's e-government project it deployed 30 videoconferencing systems in high schools and municipal governments across the islands, on a government network meant to connect 1,142 organisations; it does not split the 30 between schools and municipal governments or say in so many words that the municipal offices are on the network (no date given; page dated July 2018 from its URL).

Huawei says NOSi, the state's information society unit, initiated and implemented the e-government project, whose first phase (2010-2014) built the national data centre and upgraded the government communications network, and is responsible for its operation and maintenance (no date given; page dated July 2018 from its URL).

systems.platform: Huawei routers (530) and switches (669); videoconferencing systems (30)
systems.tiers: meant to connect 1,142 organisations: schools, medical institutions, government agencies and enterprises in small and medium-sized cities and towns; videoconferencing in high schools and municipal governments

systems.platform: Huawei cloud data centre, 1,000 virtual machines and 1,000 TB after phase 2
NOSi's framework for building government application software
